h1:
Where to Stay in Saraburi?
12 Hotels We Actually Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites!
heroSub: 12 hand-picked Saraburi hotels across every budget — golf resorts and boutiques at the foot of Khao Yai on the Muak Lek side, a riverside resort on the Pa Sak in Kaeng Khoi, a dam-side stay at Wang Muang, and budget hotels in the town centre and Phra Phutthabat. From roughly ฿550–2,200/night.
introH2: ⛰️ Why does choosing the right area in Saraburi matter so much?
introHtml: Saraburi is a gateway town on the way to Isan and the northern doorway to Khao Yai, so most people stay a single night in passing — but stays are actually spread across several areas with very different feels. Stays fall into four sides — Muak Lek, at the foot of Khao Yai, is the standout resort zone, with cooler air, near Muak Lek Waterfall, dairy farms and the Pak Chong approach to Khao Yai; Kaeng Khoi sits right on the Mittraphap (Friendship) Highway, with riverside resorts on the Pa Sak and budget boutiques; Wang Muang, furthest north by the Pa Sak Jolasid Dam, suits anyone after a quiet riverside stay; and the Saraburi town centre and Phra Phutthabat suit temple visits and overnight stops in passing. Many people book without checking the area and end up driving farther back and forth than they expected. This guide rounds up 12 hand-picked Saraburi hotels across every tier — all with real guest reviews, prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Saraburi has no metro and no commercial airport — there's a railway station in town plus buses and vans from Bangkok, but the standout resort zones of Muak Lek and Wang Muang really need a car as they sit well out of the town centre. Pick by your itinerary: Muak Lek is about 35–40 km from town, near Muak Lek Waterfall, dairy farms, vineyards and the Pak Chong approach to Khao Yai, with cooler air than in town; Kaeng Khoi sits on the Mittraphap Highway with riverside resorts on the Pa Sak, easy to stop at along the way; Wang Muang is north by the Pa Sak Jolasid Dam, about 50–60 km from town, ideal for a riverside stay; and the town centre–Phra Phutthabat is near the railway station, the mall and Wat Phra Phutthabat, best for overnight stops and travellers without a car. Almost every stay has free parking, so they suit self-drivers well.

entries.storyHtml: Sir James is the most-reviewed resort in this guide, with 2,750 reviews and a score of 8.2. It's a golf resort at the foot of Khao Yai on the Muak Lek side — spacious grounds with a golf course, a pool and mountain views. Rooms range from Panorama rooms with golf-course-view balconies to suites for families, starting around ฿1,900. It suits self-drivers coming to unwind near Khao Yai, play a round of golf, or travel as a group.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget stretches, pick a New Deluxe Room — they're more recently renovated, in better shape and with more open mountain views than the original Panorama rooms.

faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about Saraburi hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in around Saraburi?
faq.a: It depends on your itinerary and whether you have a car. Muak Lek, at the foot of Khao Yai, is the standout resort zone, with cooler air, near the waterfall and dairy farms (Sir James, The Organery, Baan Ingkhao, Muak Lek Forest, Muaklek Paradise). Kaeng Khoi sits on the Mittraphap Highway with riverside resorts on the Pa Sak (Supalai Pasak, The Bua). Wang Muang is by the Pa Sak Dam, ideal for a riverside stay (Phufa Pasak, Sakura). And the town centre–Phra Phutthabat suits en-route stops and travellers without a car (Saraburi Garden, PS Hotel, River Residence).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Saraburi hotels cost?
faq.a: Saraburi has a wide range: budget 2-star stays from around ฿550–900 (Sakura, PS Hotel, River Residence, Saraburi Garden); 3-star resorts and boutiques by the hills around ฿1,200–2,200 (Baan Ingkhao, Phufa Pasak, Muak Lek Forest, The Organery, Muaklek Paradise); and 4-star riverside and golf resorts around ฿1,600–1,900 (Supalai Pasak, Sir James).

faq.q: ❓ Can I stay in Muak Lek and visit Khao Yai?
faq.a: Yes. Muak Lek sits at the foot of Khao Yai on the Saraburi side, with a drive to the park's Pak Chong approach, and Muak Lek Waterfall, dairy farms and vineyards to stop at along the way. The standout stays here are Sir James Resort (a golf resort), The Organery Retreat (a boutique scoring 8.8) and Baan Ingkhao (garden villas) — all best with a car.

faq.q: ❓ Does Saraburi have riverside or dam-side stays?
faq.a: Yes. Supalai Pasak Resort & Spa from ฿1,600 is a bungalow resort on the Pa Sak River on the Kaeng Khoi side, with a spa and a pool, scoring 8.8. Phufa Pasak Resort from ฿1,200 has earth houses and tents with views over the Pa Sak Jolasid reservoir on the Wang Muang side — ideal for those who like being close to nature and watching the sunset over the water.

faq.q: ❓ No car, coming to Wat Phra Phutthabat — where's handy?
faq.a: If you're coming to pay respects at Wat Phra Phutthabat or stopping over in town, PS Hotel Saraburi from ฿600 is in the Phra Phutthabat area near the temple, while River Residence from ฿700 and Saraburi Garden Resort from ฿900 are in the Saraburi town centre. The resort zones of Muak Lek and Wang Muang really need a car.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Saraburi hotel?
faq.a: On regular weekdays, 1–2 weeks ahead is enough. But in the cool-season run-up (Nov–Jan) and on long weekends, stays in the Muak Lek–Khao Yai zone and by the Pa Sak Dam fill up fast — with people heading to Khao Yai and chasing the cool weather — so book 2–4 weeks ahead or more.
